comparison: Both strongly support the model characterization (C46-C51). OpenEval focuses on specific experimental evidence (immunofluorescence, saliva collection, histology), while peer reviewers emphasize the overall quality and innovation of the model, with unanimous affirmation across all three reviewers.

Both support reduced secretion findings (C52-C54). OpenEval provides detailed statistical validation, while peer reviewers incorporate these claims into broader model validation. Peer review R1 groups secretion data with model characterization claims.

Both strongly support enhanced Ca2+ signaling findings (C56, C67-C72). OpenEval emphasizes quantitative parameters and statistical significance, while peer reviewers highlight the technical innovation and surprising nature of the paradoxical findings. All reviewers accept these observations without question.

Both support disrupted Ca2+ gradient findings (C57, C75-C83). OpenEval provides detailed spatial analysis validation, while peer reviewers acknowledge these findings as part of the broader Ca2+ imaging results. Peer review groups these with other Ca2+ observations.

Both rate C84 as UNCERTAIN. OpenEval questions the causal relationship between enhanced Ca2+ signals and reduced secretion. Peer Reviewer 1 explicitly challenges whether increased Ca2+ compensates for IP3R-TMEM16a separation and notes the point was not directly addressed. Perfect agreement on uncertainty.

Both support findings that TMEM16a and AQP5 expression/localization are unchanged (C86-C89). OpenEval validates specific experimental evidence, while peer reviewers emphasize these as effectively ruling out alternative explanations for reduced secretion. Strong agreement.

Both support reduced CCh-evoked currents findings (C90-C92). OpenEval validates electrophysiological controls, while peer reviewers incorporate these into broader evidence that intrinsic TMEM16a function is unaltered. Agreement on experimental findings.

Both support that TMEM16a channel properties are unaltered (C93-C94). OpenEval validates direct Ca2+ activation experiments, while peer reviewers cite this as supporting impaired stimulus-secretion coupling rather than channel dysfunction. Agreement on findings.

Both support BAPTA/EGTA differential buffering findings (C95-C97). OpenEval validates the experimental design with caveat about kinetics assumptions, while Peer Reviewer 1 explicitly states this supports the idea that increased IP3R-TMEM16a distance contributes to secretory defect. Strong agreement.

Both support STED microscopy findings of increased IP3R3-TMEM16a distance (C98-C104). OpenEval validates quantitative measurements and statistical analysis, while all three peer reviewers explicitly affirm these findings as key evidence for disrupted microdomain coupling. Unanimous agreement.

Both address mitochondrial morphology changes (C110-C114). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED based on quantitative metrics, while peer reviewers acknowledge the observations but Reviewer 1 questions their integration and mechanistic significance, rating overall mitochondrial findings as UNCERTAIN.

Both address ultrastructural mitochondrial changes (C115-C121). OpenEval supports based on detailed EM quantification, while peer reviewers acknowledge findings but Reviewer 1 states they are 'largely descriptive' and not well-integrated mechanistically. Divergence on interpretation significance.

Both address mitochondrial functional impairment (C124-C130). OpenEval supports based on TMRE and Seahorse data convergence, while peer reviewers acknowledge observations but question mechanistic connection to secretory deficits. Reviewer 1 states 'more studies are needed to connect them.'

Both address integrative conclusions about mechanisms (C15, C64-C65). OpenEval supports Ca2+-TMEM16a link but notes speculative elements about mitochondria. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 1 stating mitochondrial role 'was not examined' and Reviewer 3 noting 'exact contribution...remains to be determined.' Agreement on uncertainty of mitochondrial causality.

OpenEval supports model utility claims (C131-C132, C135) based on demonstrated early SS features. Peer reviewers implicitly support through unanimous praise of model characterization, though they don't separately evaluate these specific utility claims.
OpenEval supports claims about STIM1 expression and disease stage interpretation (C136-C139). No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific comparative claims.

OpenEval rates speculative mechanistic hypotheses (C140-C143) as UNCERTAIN, noting they lack direct experimental support. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these speculative claims.
OpenEval rates alternative mechanism claims about oxidative stress (C133-C134) as UNCERTAIN. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these off-target effect considerations.

OpenEval supports AQP5 negative finding (C145) based on study data and human study citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses this claim, though peer R4 mentions AQP5 in broader context.
OpenEval supports translational relevance of EM findings to human patients (C157). No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses this translational claim.
OpenEval supports background/contextual claims (C1-C3, C35-C37) as appropriate scientific framing. No corresponding peer review evaluation addresses these introductory context claims.

Peer review R2 includes claims C6, C56, C57 (in addition to Ca2+ imaging claims covered by OpenEval R3 and R4). These broader framing claims about the paradox are not separately evaluated by OpenEval but are incorporated into R3's evaluation.

Peer review R4 includes claims C7, C58 (broader framing about ruling out alternatives) that are not separately evaluated by OpenEval, though the specific experimental findings (C86-C94) are covered by OpenEval R6, R7, and R8.

Peer review R5 includes claims C9-C11, C59-C60 (broader framing about microdomain coupling mechanism) that are not separately evaluated by OpenEval, though the specific experimental findings are covered by OpenEval R9 and R10.

Peer review R6 includes claims C13-C14, C61-C63 (broader framing about mitochondrial dysfunction) that are not separately evaluated by OpenEval, though specific experimental findings are covered by OpenEval R11, R12, and R13.

Peer review R7 includes claim C66 (about bidirectional Ca2+-mitochondria relationship) not separately evaluated by OpenEval. Reviewer 3 notes 'exact contribution of calcium and mitochondria to secretory dysfunction remains to be determined.'
